document.title: Mahmud Plans 2nd Mission to Afghanistan (Islamabad 05123)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), "No-Go" Tribal Areas Became Basis for Afghan Insurgency Documents Show
document.note: [Secret] ISI Director Mahmoud tells Ambassador Chamberlin he is returning to Afghanistan to make a last plea to the Taliban. He believes a negotiated solution is preferable and urges her "not to act in anger. Real victory will come in negotiations." He says it is better for the Afghans to deal with bin Laden and warns of warlordism if the Taliban are eliminated. Chamberlin replies that Omar has refused every U.S. demand and the trip cannot delay military planning.

events.description: Mahmud's first meeting with Mullah Omar; Omar intransigent.
Planned second Mahmud trip to meet Omar, possibly with Pakistani religious leaders, to press demands on bin Laden, Shelter Now detainees and camps.

Mahmud planned a second trip to Afghanistan to meet Omar, possibly with Pakistani religious leaders.

Pakistan planned to withdraw remaining diplomats from Afghanistan within 48 hours and was considering severing relations.

key_claims: Mahmud planned a second mission to Mullah Omar, about September 25, 2001, to press for surrender of bin Laden and release of Shelter Now detainees.
Mahmud said Omar was frightened and the Taliban weak, but that US strikes would create an incubator of anger.
The Embassy judged Mahmud had virtually no chance of success but did not oppose the effort so long as it did not delay military planning.
Pakistan feared Taliban elimination would create a political vacuum and warlordism.
The mission also served Musharraf's domestic interests by showing a peaceful solution was sought.
